messages:
maria: Heads-up — following last night's degraded capacity in eu-west we sketched a small PR for a conditional failover flow that prefers warm-pool routing before/global weighted shifts. Want feedback before I open the runbook change. :memo:

jules: Thanks. Can you paste the decision tree? want to check abort conditions and cost throttle limits. :eyes:

maria: Sure — rough snippet below. The idea is: only escalate to cross-region shift if warm-pool spare GPUs < 10% and avg latency > 2s for 5m. Also add a cost-safeguard that halts cross-region shifts if projected spend delta > 30% of baseline for the hour.

```
if warm_pool_spare_pct >= 10% and latency_5m < 2s:
  route -> warm_pool
elif warm_pool_spare_pct < 10% and projected_spend_delta <= 30%:
  do weighted_shift(region_candidates, max_shift=20%)
elif projected_spend_delta > 30%:
  increase_local_backpressure(); notify(@oncall);
else:
  escalate_to_manual_failover()
```

sam: Love the cost throttle. A couple of notes:
- projected_spend_delta needs a clear calc (incurred tokens + egress + burst GPU hours).
- define who is the approver for manual_failover (SRE oncall + infra lead?).

alex: Also add a safety check for model-compat variants. If we fall back to a quantized variant, mark traffic as lower-qa and route only traffic tagged non-critical.

kevin: Quick ops checklist I suggest adding to the runbook under "pre-shift validation":
- confirm control-plane is reachable from target region (ping / curl headers)
- confirm routing table prop delay < 60s
- confirm KV cache compatibility (model hash match)
- validate warm-pool health >= 2/3 nodes

maria: Good checklist — I'll slot that in. For manual approvers let's make it: oncall + infra lead for automatic escalations above 50% shift. For <=50% we allow SRE oncall to approve within 10m.

jules: Can we add a non-blocking smoke test to run immediately after shift? e.g., fire 50 synthetic requests with golden prompts and check response latency/quality pass rate > 98%. If failing, automatically roll back.

maria: Yep. Proposed smoke command to embed in runbook:

```bash
# run smoke test against new-route
python infra/tests/smoke_runner.py --region ams --requests 50 --golden tests/golden_set.json --timeout 30s
exit_code=$?
if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
  rollback_shift --reason smoke-failure
  alert #incident-channel
fi
```

ops-bot: auto-note: added TODO tag to runbook PR #418 (maria) — awaiting approvals.

sam: A few extra action items for post-incident follow-up (to add as bullet list in runbook):
- run cost simulation tool weekly for 'what-if' 3x/5x surge patterns
- add a metric for "shift-induced latency delta" to detect oscillations
- add per-customer tag to avoid shifting heavy enterprise tenants without consent

kevin: Agree. Also add a command snippet to preview projected spend for a candidate shift: 

```json
# example payload to cost-sim service
{ "region_from": "ams", "region_to": "iad", "percent_shift": 15, "duration_minutes": 60 }
```

maria: I will draft the PR with these pieces tonight. Will include an ops playbook section: Purpose, Decision tree, Pre-shift checklist, Smoke tests, Cost throttle, Manual escalation matrix, Post-shift validations.

jules: Nice. Can you assign reviewers: sam, kevin, alex? Also tag @security for egress policy implications when moving cross-region.

maria: Assigned. PR will be up by 09:00 UTC. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: One last operational concern — make sure the weighted_shift code honors per-queue affinity so we don't split long-lived streaming sessions mid-shift. Add a drain grace-period param (default 90s).

alex: noted, i'll add a liveness-check to avoid split sessions.

ops-bot: incident-note: follow-up task created: "conditional-failover-playbook PR" assigned to maria, reviewers sam,kevin,alex; due 3 days.

maria: I'll post a short summary in #eng-sre once PR merges and schedule a dry-run for next maintenance window.

kevin: +1, schedule the dry-run with a small canary in eu-west and one in ap-south.

maria: End of thread — collecting these as runbook edits and action items.
